sn.c: Orchestra rows P to R can feel quite far back due to the auditorium's deep but narrow design.
sn.sh: Rows P to R can feel quite far back

sn.c: Seats and legroom can be very tight, especially in the Mezzanine.
sn.sh: Mezzanine seats and legroom can be tight

sn.c: Mezzanine row A in the middle section offers a great view of the stage from an elevated position.
sn.sh: Elevated stage view from Mezzanine row A

sn.c: The back few Mezzanine rows can be considered the least desirable, but views are still good compared with equivalent seats in larger Broadway theaters.
sn.sh: Back Mezzanine views are still good

sn.c: For extra legroom in the Orchestra, pick row A or an aisle seat.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's smallest houses (597 seats) and one of its newest, built in 2015 as Second Stage's permanent home. The intimate scale means excellent sightlines from nearly every seat, though the modern design prioritizes function over grandeur.

acc.note: Elevator from lower lobby to Mezzanine. LOOP system for t-coils and cochlear implants.
